statement: Does there exist a k such that every sufficiently large integer can be written in the form \prod_{i=1}^{k} a_i - \sum_{i=1}^{k} a_i for some integers a_i >= 2?
notes: The problem is RESOLVED IN THE AFFIRMATIVE: yes, such a k exists — in fact a small fixed k already works for every sufficiently large integer (indeed for all integers, with the right threshold), via a simple explicit construction observed by Eli Seamans. Formalize the affirmative assertion (existence of k and of the threshold N). The a_i need not be distinct. 'Integer' here can be taken as n ranging over integers (or naturals) that are sufficiently large; each a_i is an integer >= 2. Beware: over the naturals, subtraction truncates — prefer stating the equation over the integers to keep the subtraction honest.
